chapter: New Orleans pianists and Clarence Williams
title: Tony Jackson and Arthur Campbell
summary: Robichaux says Tony Jackson was a wonderful pianist despite his entertainer's reputation, and Arthur Campbell good too.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah, he was a good piano player. O'Neal was a good piano player. And also there was another piano player, oh he played nice piano too, and he was playing in the district during the time when ... Did you ever hear Tony Jackson? Oh, Tony Jackson. He was good. Yeah, I heard Tony Jackson, Louis Wade, Fred Washington, and I'm trying to think of this other piano player. I heard them all three playing in a house at one time, you know, one take time. Yeah. And he was a very good piano player. And then the next time I heard him was in Chicago, he used to play at the E-Light when I went up to Chicago.
Some people have told me he was a wonderful pianist, and others say well he was mostly a good singer and entertainer. Was he a wonderful pianist?

No, he was a wonderful piano player, you see. People say that, you see, because he was an entertainer and he could be talking and holding a conversation and talk to anybody and just go ahead and play what he was playing and he never missed a note and just be talking about anything and don't look at the piano. But some people say oh he was a good entertainer, but he was a good piano player, period. Yeah. Yeah, he was a good piano player.
He wrote a lot of good numbers too, like Play Baby and ...
Yeah, yeah, he actually was a good piano player. And they had Arthur Campbell too.
Oh yes. I don't know him, but I mean ...
Yeah, he was a nice piano player. He went to Chicago, I think he died in Chicago too.
He made one record with Freddie Keppert.
